$comment: DXpeditions: one-shot operations, NOT contests. Kept in a separate file from contests.seed.json on purpose -- a DXpedition has no recurrence rule, no exchange and no eligibility question, and forcing it into a contest record would make every one of those fields conditional and stop 'contest' meaning what it means. The recurrence engine is not involved at all: these are plain UTC day ranges, so nothing here touches the Python/TypeScript parity suite.
sourcing_rule: Same rule as the contest catalog, and it bites harder here. Populate a record ONLY from the expedition's own site. NG3K's ADXO, DX-World, DXZone, dxping and the rest are aggregators -- use them to LEARN THAT AN OPERATION EXISTS and to find its site, never as the source of its dates.

field_notes.precision: 'exact' -- the team published start and end days. 'approximate' -- the team published enough to BOUND the window but not the days themselves, typically a departure date plus a travel estimate plus a duration. Plotted on the calendar, because refusing to show an operation that is on the air fails the reader, but marked everywhere it appears so it is never mistaken for a published schedule. The record's note must show the arithmetic. 'month' -- only a month or a season has been announced, the normal state until a few weeks out. NEVER plotted: placing it on days nobody announced would invent the one fact a reader came for. Listed on /dx with the window as stated.
field_notes.start/end: Whole UTC days, not instants. A DXpedition runs around the clock for its duration and teams do not publish an hour, so an hour is not recorded. This is why the month grid suits them: it buckets by UTC day already.
field_notes.ended: Set true once the operation is over. The record stays -- the site's own page often goes dark or turns into a QRT notice within months, so this calendar becomes the surviving statement of when it ran.
field_notes.bands/modes: Same invariant as contests: EMPTY MEANS UNRECORDED, not unrestricted. Most teams publish a band plan on a page of its own, and where it has not been read the list stays empty and every band filter excludes the record.

dxpeditions.name: Franz Josef Land
dxpeditions.source_note: rudxt.org/ri1fjl, the Russian DXpedition Team's own page for the operation. Heiss Island, Franz Josef Land, IOTA EU-019, which the team calls 'the northernmost DXCC in the world'. Six operators: R7AL (leader), UA3QLC, RW8A, UA4Z, RA4DX and RW9JZ. Modes and stations: they will 'run ... at least 5 high-power stations 24/7 on all HF bands' in CW, SSB and FT8. QSL by direct OQRS through ClubLog, bureau available. Timing as the team states it: 'The departure is scheduled on the 7-th of August 2026 from Murmansk', 'Estimated travel time is 6-7 days', and the operation runs 'for 15 days'. Checked 2026-08-23.
dxpeditions.note:
APPROXIMATE, AND HERE IS THE ARITHMETIC. The team did not publish a start day or an end day -- they published a departure, a crossing and a duration. Departure 7 August plus the stated 6-7 days at sea puts them ashore on 13 or 14 August; 15 days of operating from there ends on 28 or 29 August. This record holds 13 to 29 August, which is the widest window the team's own numbers support, and it is marked approximate everywhere it appears rather than presented as a schedule.

IT IS ALSO WEATHER-DEPENDENT AND THE TEAM SAYS SO: 'Fingers crossed that the coastal strip will be free of ice.' A landing on Franz Josef Land is not a certainty even after the crossing.

BANDS ARE UNRECORDED. 'All HF bands' is the team's phrasing, and this catalog does not turn a phrase into a band list -- the same reason JARL's New Year Party and the ZS SOTA weekend carry none. Every band filter therefore excludes this record.

AN ANNOUNCEMENT LIST DISAGREES WITH THE ARITHMETIC, AND THAT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN RESOLVED. NG3K's ADXO shows this operation as 22-29 August. The team's own page supports 13-14 August ashore, and a separate report has them leaving Murmansk on 12 August rather than the 7th announced, which would push the landing later still. Three numbers, one of them from a source this project does not take dates from. The window here stays as the team's own figures bound it and this note says plainly that the start day is not settled; the end, 29 August, is the one point all three agree on.
dxpeditions.summary: Six operators on Heiss Island, Franz Josef Land -- the northernmost DXCC entity -- with five high-power stations running around the clock on CW, SSB and FT8.

dxpeditions.name: Christmas Island
dxpeditions.team: Pacific Islands DXpedition Group (PIDXG) with YOTA
dxpeditions.source_note: vk9xy2026.com, the team's own site: 'On the air November 16 - December 4, 2026.' The operation is Christmas Island, IOTA OC-002, run by the Pacific Islands DXpedition Group in partnership with YOTA (Youngsters On The Air) and led by Max Freedman, N4ML. Checked 2026-08-23.
dxpeditions.note: BANDS AND MODES ARE NOT RECORDED YET. The team's front page states the dates and the entity but no band plan, and this catalog does not guess one -- an invented band list on a nineteen-day operation would be read as a schedule. The consequence is the usual one and the pages say it: every band filter excludes this record until someone reads the team's band plan.
dxpeditions.summary: Nineteen days from Christmas Island, run by the Pacific Islands DXpedition Group with a youth team.

dxpeditions.name: South Georgia
dxpeditions.entity: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands
dxpeditions.source_note: ardxpeditions.com/dxpeditions/vp0sg, the team's own page. The permit is granted and the timing is a month, not dates: an August 2026 update states VP0SG 'is authorised to conduct its planned amateur radio operations at Husvik, South Georgia, in March 2027'. No start or end day has been published. Checked 2026-08-23.
dxpeditions.note: MONTH PRECISION, WHICH IS WHY IT IS NOT ON THE CALENDAR. The team has announced March 2027 and nothing narrower. Drawing it across the whole of March would claim thirty-one days of operation nobody announced, and drawing it on a guessed fortnight would invent the one fact a reader came for. It is listed with the window as stated and moves onto the calendar the day the team publishes days. This is the normal state of a DXpedition until a few weeks out -- most are announced by month first. BANDS AND MODES ARE ALSO UNRECORDED, and for the same reason as the dates: the team has a permit and a month, and has not published a band plan. Empty means unread here exactly as it does in the contest catalog, so every band filter excludes this record.
dxpeditions.summary: A permitted operation from Husvik, South Georgia, announced for March 2027 with dates still to come.

dxpeditions.name: Franz Josef Land
dxpeditions.team: Russian Arctic National Park expedition (RA1ZZ, R9LR)
dxpeditions.source_note: ri1fjz.ru/en/, the team's own site. Aleksandry Island, Franz Josef Land, IOTA EU-019. Dates as printed: '09.09.2026 - 25.09.2026'. Bands and modes: '160, 80, 40, 30, 20, 17, 15, 12, 10 m, VHF bands and satellites' with 'CW, SSB, FT-8 (Normal mode, Fox mode MSHV software)', including QO-100. Led by RA1ZZ (Vasily) and R9LR (Vladimir) with the support of the Russian Arctic National Park. 'QSL via: R9LR', and the 'Full DXpedition log will uploaded to Club Log and LoTW'. Checked 2026-08-23.
dxpeditions.note:
THE BANDS ARE ENUMERATED HERE BECAUSE THE TEAM ENUMERATED THEM -- nine HF bands listed one by one, WARC included. That is a list rather than a phrase, so it is recorded as one, unlike H49A and XR0Z below whose teams wrote 'all HF bands' and '160 to 10 meters' and left the WARC question open.

The team also names 'VHF bands and satellites' including QO-100 without listing which, so that stays in bands_note. VHF is out of scope for sourcing new contests; it is not a reason to truncate what a team says about its own operation.

THE SECOND FRANZ JOSEF LAND OPERATION IN A MONTH, and a different one: RI1FJL was Heiss Island in August, this is Aleksandry Island in September, different teams and different callsigns. Same DXCC entity, same IOTA group.
dxpeditions.bands_note: The team also lists 'VHF bands and satellites', including QO-100, without naming which.
dxpeditions.summary: Seventeen days from Aleksandry Island, Franz Josef Land, on nine HF bands plus satellite, with the Russian Arctic National Park's support.

dxpeditions.name: Solomon Islands
dxpeditions.source_note: solomon2026.com, the team's own site: 'October 9th - October 21st 2026', 'all HF bands + 6m, CW, SSB and FT8'. Led by Rolando 9A3MR with Zrinko DK8ZZ/YT3ZZ, Mladen 9A2NA, Frane 9A3CJY, Kristijan 9A4WY and Livio 9A7Y. Checked 2026-08-23.
dxpeditions.note:
BANDS UNRECORDED BECAUSE 'ALL HF BANDS' IS A PHRASE, NOT A LIST. It leaves the WARC bands open and this catalog does not turn a phrase into a band list -- the same treatment JARL's New Year Party and the ZS SOTA weekend get. Every band filter therefore excludes this record until someone reads a published band plan.

NG3K'S ANNOUNCEMENT LIST SAYS 7-21 OCTOBER; THE TEAM SAYS THE 9TH. The team's own site wins, as it must. Recorded here because the two disagree and a reader comparing them should know which this calendar followed.
dxpeditions.bands_note: The team says 'all HF bands + 6m' without naming them.
dxpeditions.summary: Thirteen days from the Solomon Islands by a Croatian team, CW, SSB and FT8 across the HF bands and 6 m.

dxpeditions.name: Juan Fernández
dxpeditions.source_note: xr0z.net, the team's own site. Alexander Selkirk Island, Juan Fernández, IOTA SA-101. Timing as stated: 'approximately 10 days during October 2026'. Bands and modes: 160 to 10 metres in FT8, CW and SSB. Moisés CE3VTZ and Felipe XQ7IR; QSL via M0URX. Checked 2026-08-23.
dxpeditions.note:
MONTH PRECISION, AND VAGUER THAN MOST: 'approximately 10 days during October 2026' gives a month and a duration but no start. Ten days inside a thirty-one-day window has twenty-two possible starts, so it is listed and not plotted -- putting it on a guessed fortnight would invent the one fact a reader came for. It moves onto the calendar the day the team names days.

BANDS UNRECORDED: '160 to 10 meters' is a span rather than a list and leaves WARC open. RI1FJZ's team enumerated its nine bands and that record has them; this one did not.
dxpeditions.bands_note: The team says '160 to 10 meters' without naming the bands.
dxpeditions.summary: About ten days from Alexander Selkirk Island in the Juan Fernández group, with the days still to be announced.
